description:
The fatal arm of 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN reached with a status of '22', and the case that completes this program's open-status matrix. app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl:118-134 is deliberately two-armed: :121 asks whether CARDFILE-STATUS is '00' and nothing else, so every other status - '22' among them - falls through to :124 MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT. There is no APPL-EOF arm in the open paragraph; that exists only in the read paragraph at :107. The guard at :126 therefore fails APPL-AOK and runs its ELSE in source order: DISPLAY 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE' at :129, MOVE CARDFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS at :130, PERFORM 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS at :131, and PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM at :132, which DISPLAYs 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at :155, moves 0 into TIMING at :156 and 999 into ABCODE at :157, and CALLs 'CEE3ABD' at :158. A duplicate-key condition on an OPEN is unusual, and that is exactly the point: the paragraph does not classify the status, it only compares it to '00', so an implementation that routed a duplicate somewhere gentler - or that shared one status-handling routine between the open and the read, where :98 genuinely does treat '10' as an orderly end - would not abend here at all. This is the open-side counterpart of case12, which reports the same '22' on the first READ and reaches a different paragraph with it. Exactly four lines are emitted, and no more. The abend at :158 terminates the run unit where it stands, so nothing after :132 in the mainline runs: the read loop at :74-81 is never entered, no 150-character CARD-RECORD image is ever displayed at :78, 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE at :83 never issues its CLOSE, and the closing banner at :85 is never emitted. Both absences are the assertion, not an omission from it. SYSOUT is therefore precisely these four lines, of 38, 22, 24 and 16 characters, every width counted from the literal in the source rather than assumed. The return code is 12, from :124, carried out of the program unchanged by the abend. Neither of the program's other two APPL-RESULT values can be observed here. The 8 that :119 moves in before the OPEN is a transient assumption of failure that :122 or :124 always overwrites before :126 tests it, so no run can end on it. The 16 is the 88 APPL-EOF marker declared at :63 and moved only at :99 on the read path, which this case never reaches. Only 0 and 12 are reachable return codes anywhere in CBACT02C. ABCODE 999 and TIMING 0 are the two Language Environment abend parameters the service reads at :156-157 and are never the return code. The status line: 01 IO-STATUS-04 is IO-STATUS-0401 PIC 9 followed by IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999 at :57-59, four bytes in all. '22' is numeric and its first byte is not '9', so 9910 takes its ELSE at :169-172: MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04 leaves positions one and two holding their zeros, MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2) lands the two status characters on the one-based positions three and four, and the image is 0022. DISPLAY concatenates its operands with no separator, so the emitted line is the 20-character literal 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' immediately followed by those four digits - 24 characters in total, with no space between the NNNN and the 0022. That trailing NNNN really is part of the hard-coded literal at :168 and :172 rather than a placeholder awaiting substitution, and it is reproduced verbatim: tidying it into 'FILE STATUS IS: 0022' would be a behaviour change, so the oddity stands. What "inputs" says, and what it does not. The whole card master is seeded on the binding key CARDFILE and not one of its fifty rows is read, which is the same declaration the other four failing-open cases make: a dataset can exist, and be full, and still refuse to open. That is deliberately not case02's statement. case02 declares "empty": true with its 150-byte "recordLength" and the "copybook" CVACT02Y, which positively asserts that a real dataset was opened and reached end of file on its first READ - it opens successfully and completes normally with return code 0 and no error line at all. Nor is it the third possibility: DatasetInput admits exactly one of "rows", "fixture" or "empty": true and has no member for an unavailable dataset, so a dataset that is not there at all can only be declared by omitting it from "inputs" altogether. Seeded-but-refused, present-but-empty and absent are three different assertions, and this case makes the first. A note on '35', recorded rather than silently resolved. A z/OS OPEN INPUT of a non-optional dataset that is not present reports FILE STATUS '35', which through the same ELSE arm would render 0, 0, 3, 5 and give FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0035 - also 24 characters. This translation cannot report it. AccountBalanceReaderJob's open calls CardRepository.openBrowse and reads the CICS response the returned browse handle carries, and FileStatus.batchStatusOfCicsResp translates only NORMAL to '00', ENDFILE to '10', NOTFND to '23' and DUPREC or DUPKEY to '22', answering empty for every other response because inventing a two-character batch counterpart for a response that has none would invent behaviour the COBOL never had; an empty answer lands on the '9' permanent-error convention instead, which is the image case09 and case10 assert. '35' is therefore outside the set of status images this program can emit, and the divergence from the mainframe is recorded here rather than papered over. The two-character status this case does force is '22', at the openBrowse call site - openBrowse and not startBrowse, because startBrowse is the online entry point that issues no backend call and reports no status at all, so an open tested through it would leave :129-132 unreachable and an unusable dataset would first appear as 'ERROR READING CARDFILE' on the following read. The unit is account.AccountBalanceReaderJob, whose name and package are prompt-mandated and whose behaviour is not: it is called Account and sits in the account package, but CBACT02C reads the CARD file - :29 ASSIGNs CARDFILE and :39-40 declares a 16-byte key over 134 bytes of data - and this case, like every other in this directory, exercises the card master alone. It is driven at the tasklet body, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP in the path. No job parameter is declared, because app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:22 is a bare EXEC PGM=CBACT02C with no PARM. Nothing is written, so no write and no surviving dataset state is reported. No fully-qualified dataset name appears anywhere: a case addresses a dataset only by its binding key. Every line is US-ASCII, the code page of app/data/ASCII and of the harness's fixture charset, never a platform default. The case is deterministic - a fixed status, a fixed line list, no wall-clock and no random value. Provenance: statically derived by structured reading of app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl, cross-checked against app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy for the 150-byte record the loop would have displayed and app/jcl/READCARD.jcl for the DD name and the absence of a PARM, and against the constants AccountBalanceReaderJob, AbendException and FileStatus publish. Nothing here was captured from a run of the legacy COBOL, which is impossible in this environment - there is no z/OS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, and no Language Environment CEE service exists to link the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at :158 - and that substitution of provenance, and nothing else about the gate, is the escalated deviation recorded as risk R-A. Because a BATCH_JOB case cannot declare a forced repository outcome - ParityCase refuses a screenRequest on one - the inducement of the '22' open status is wired by CBACT02CParityTest's per-case scenario rather than by this file, which states only the fingerprint the run must produce.

HOW THE OUTCOME IS ARRANGED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. This case arranges an OPEN that reports DFHRESP(DUPREC) on the base key: unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes names OPEN-CARDFILE and gives it RESP 14. It is declared here because a case identifier must name a case and never configure one - the shape used to be chosen by a switch over 'case01'..'case20' in CBACT02CParityTest, so this file showed the abend lines and said nothing about the condition that produced them, and renumbering a case silently changed what it ran. A case that names no call site reads its whole input and closes cleanly, so silence here is itself a statement. The outcome is a CICS RESP rather than a FILE STATUS because CardRepository reports this program's card-file outcomes as responses and AccountBalanceReaderJob translates them - declaring a status directly would skip the translation the case exists to judge.
